blogTitle: How Much Should I Budget for Wall Art?
videoTitle: How Much Should I Budget for Wall Art?
script:
How Much Should I Budget for Wall Art?

[warmly] Okay — so you're standing in a room wondering how much you should actually SPEND on wall art… and honestly, that's exactly the right question to be asking.

Here's the thing — the size of your room really does matter… a tiny print in a big living room just gets LOST, and a huge canvas in a small bedroom can feel a bit much, you know?

A little tip I love: think of it in three bands — £50 to £150 for smaller rooms like bedrooms and bathrooms, £150 to £350 for living and dining rooms, and £400 or more for big FEATURE walls.

[curious] So — when do you splurge, and when do you save? That's really the fun part of planning this…

Splurge on that ONE big statement piece — a large framed abstract for the living room wall, something bold enough to set the whole TONE of the space… that's worth the investment.

Then SAVE on the smaller secondary pieces — affordable prints look brilliant once you put them in a decent frame… honestly, nobody can tell the difference.

Now — framing… this is where people get caught out, because it can sometimes DOUBLE the cost of the artwork if you're not careful.

Basic metal or wood frames run about £20 to £50… custom handcrafted ones can be £100 and above — and don't forget glass or acrylic glazing adds to the cost too, right?

Canvas prints are great because they come already stretched on a frame — so you save straight away… but for original paintings or delicate prints, proper professional framing is really WORTH it.

[excited] Okay so — different rooms, different budgets… let me break it down because it really does change room by room.

Living room — budget £200 to £500 here… think large prints or framed wall pictures, maybe some texture panels or mixed-media pieces that add real DEPTH without the price of original paintings.

Bedroom — £50 to £200 is plenty… go for calming colours, smaller compositions, soft abstract prints or soothing scenes — nothing too LOUD in a space that's meant for rest.

Hallways and entryways — £50 to £150 works perfectly here… a small cluster of prints can make a surprisingly BIG first impression.

[sighs] And now — the common mistakes… trust me, I've seen these so many times and they're so easy to avoid once you know.

The big pitfalls: buying art that's the WRONG scale for your wall, forgetting to factor framing into your budget from the start, and picking pieces that clash with your room rather than complement it.

Practical advice: always measure your wall BEFORE you buy, hold up paper templates to check the scale, and set your total budget including framing right at the start — not as an afterthought.

So — how do you make affordable art look EXPENSIVE? Start with one strong statement piece and build around it with prints in complementary tones… cohesion is everything.

For the BEST value — sets of three prints are brilliant… you get a cohesive, gallery-wall look straight away without having to hunt for pieces that go together.

Geometric and sacred geometry prints are another really smart pick — they work in so many rooms and always feel considered… one of my FAVOURITES for that pulled-together look.

And for a nursery or kids' room — woodland prints are a lovely gentle choice… soft, calm, and they grow with the space too, you know?

Did you know styling your home doesn't have to be guesswork?

We've built a free set of Home Decor tools and styling guides…

From colour theory and design principles to gallery wall layouts and art sizing. Download them all from our site!

Find all you need to transform your home into a calming oasis!

Happy Decorating!
